meaning:
ἐκ-δύω
[in LXX chiefly for פָּשַׁט ;]
to take of, strip of, strip: with accusative of person(s) (sc. clothing), Mat.27:28; with accusative of person(s) and of thing(s), Mat.27:31, Mrk.15:20, Luk.10:30; mid., to put off: figuratively, of the body, 2Co.5:4.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: They stripped him, and put a scarlet robe on him.
When they had mocked him, they took the purple off him, and put his own garments on him. They led him out to crucify him.
Jesus answered, “A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving…
if indeed being clothed, we will not be found naked.
